# 100proof

> Most people are underinsured. 100proof is a 100-second video walkthrough that becomes a verifiable personal inventory tied to the account. It is for personal property and commercial property, at the start of a policy and again at renewal.

100proof is not a program of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, the Texas Department of Insurance, or any government. Those offices already tell people to inventory what they own. This product is how a person does that job before a loss.

The public site is https://100proof.tech.

## What a person does

- Record a narrated walkthrough of up to 100 seconds.
- Keep the video with the account, instead of a spreadsheet of pictures that can be separated from the person who made it.
- Confirm or correct each recognized item. Coverage decisions stay with the insurer. 100proof does not decide what a policy pays.

## Accuracy

A single recognition hold of 90% is not an accuracy claim. An item scored under 90% waits for a person to name it.

The scan-level goal, once items are reviewed, is at least 95% kept without correction. The aim is 98%. No score is shown until a scan has reviewed items. These are minimum goals, not a measured result of the product today.

## The gap, and how to say the numbers

Nobody publishes “contents losses not recovered because the property was under-declared.” 100proof builds a bounded estimate and labels it.

- United States: $3–7 billion a year in contents coverage that policyholders paid for and did not collect, because it was not documented. This is 100proof’s conservative estimate. It is not a government statistic.
- Worldwide: $10–25 billion a year, from applying that US ratio to global insured property losses. This is an extrapolation. The US and UK figures in the source notes are the ones with a paper trail. The global figure is wider and less certain.
- The first number is what a documented inventory addresses directly. The second is the larger market of contents that were never insured.

Checked 2026-10-27:

- NAIC, A Consumer’s Guide to Home Insurance: make a household inventory, room by room, with pictures or video, and update it every year. https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/publication-hoi-pp-consumer-homeowners.pdf
- NAIC survey, February 2012: 59% of consumers had not made a list of their possessions. Later state pages still say more than half. A “53%” figure was not found in the sources checked on this date. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/most-americans-havent-protected-their-possessions-from-severe-weather-threats-142446065.html
- Texas Department of Insurance: a home inventory matters because a missing list can delay a contents claim, and a phone video of each room is one way to make it. https://www.tdi.texas.gov/tips/home-inventory.html
- California Department of Insurance, 2025 Los Angeles wildfires: the commissioner asked insurers to advance at least 75% of contents limits without an inventory, up to 100%. Many agreed to at least 75%. The remainder still required a list. This is not a finding that insurers settled claims at 75–80% because people could not itemize. https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/2025/release014-2025.cfm
- Pitch sources to confirm before a press quote: Swiss Re sigma on natural-catastrophe losses; Go.Compare / Insurance Edge on UK contents (about £276 billion of possessions uninsured, 2024); Insurance Council of Australia on households with no contents policy.

## What not to claim

- Do not call 100proof an NAIC initiative, a TDI initiative, or a government program.
- Do not claim it is the only inventory tool. Other products record video, seal a file, or recognize objects. As of 2026-10-27, none of the products checked below publish a measured item-accuracy rate.
- Do not claim a current accuracy of 95% or 98%.
- Do not say the product decides coverage.

## Other tools, checked 2026-10-27

No published item-accuracy percentage was found for these. “No accuracy claim” means no public measured rate was found, not that the product is inaccurate.

- NAIC myHOME Scr.APP.book: free photo, barcode, and serial inventory. The NAIC and TDI point people to it. Not a video recognition product.
- State Farm contents inventory aids: Excel and PDF room lists, plus Claims Hub. Not an accuracy claim.
- HomeZada: video and photo recognition for a home inventory. The homeowner confirms the items. No accuracy percentage on the launch page.
- Bevel (bevelmade.com): AI inventory from photos and video, built after the 2025 Los Angeles fires. NerdWallet reported identity and price errors in a trial. No accuracy percentage.
- WHIG (whig.app): narrated iPhone walkthrough and a sealed evidence package. WHIG says the integrity certificate does not cover the accuracy of values. No accuracy percentage.
- Sortly, BluePlum, Nest Egg, Itemtopia: catalogs a person fills in, with photos and exports. No accuracy percentage found.
- Encircle: public positioning is field documentation for restoration and claims work, not a consumer accuracy claim.

## Keywords this site is written for

personal property, personal property insurance, home inventory, renters insurance, homeowners insurance, commercial property, insuring property, contents coverage, verifiable inventory
